title: Every point of a small etale topos is geometric
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $S_{\mathrm{Et}}$ be its small etale topos [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $p:\mathbf{Set}\to S_{\mathrm{Et}}$ be a point, meaning a geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. There is a geometric point $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ [def-weil-geometric-point] such that $p$ is isomorphic to the point associated with $\bar s$. Equivalently, the inverse-image functor $p^{-1}$ is naturally isomorphic to the geometric stalk functor
$$F\longmapsto\varinjlim_{(U,\bar u)}F(U),$$
where $(U,\bar u)$ runs over pointed etale neighbourhoods of $\bar s$ and the colimit is taken over the opposite of that neighbourhood category. All fields and stalks may be taken in a common enlarged universe.

source.place: Tag 04HU, Lemma lemma-points-small-etale-site, parts (1) and (2); associated point is Tag 04FM, Lemma lemma-stalk-gives-point.

proof.text: Put $u(U)=p^{-1}(h_U^\#)$. Apply [lem-trf-site-point-reconstruction-sets] on the small skeleton of $S_{\mathrm{Et}}$ fixed by [def-weil-size-convention]. It supplies preservation of finite limits, joint surjectivity for covers, and reconstruction of $p^{-1}$ from the pointed $u$-objects. In particular $u(S)$ is a singleton and $u(\varnothing)=\varnothing$ (the empty covering). An open immersion gives an injection on $u$, since it is a monomorphism and $u$ preserves its diagonal pullback. For any disjoint union $T=\coprod T_i$, the covering by the summands gives a surjection $\coprod u(T_i)\to u(T)$. It is injective: different summands have empty intersection, and the diagonal pullback proves injectivity within each summand. Thus $u(T)=\coprod u(T_i)$ via the inclusions.

source.place: Tag 04HU, lemma-points-small-etale-site; first paragraph (site/topos comparison and fibre functor properties).

proof.text:
For an open $O\subset S$, the set $u(O)$ has at most one element. Let $W$ be the union of all opens with empty $u$-value. The open cover of $W$ by these opens gives $u(W)=\varnothing$. Set $Z=S\setminus W$; it is nonempty because $u(S)
e\varnothing$. If $Z=Z_1\cup Z_2$ for closed subsets of $S$, then $W=(S\setminus Z_1)\cap(S\setminus Z_2)$. Preservation of intersections implies that one of $u(S\setminus Z_i)$ is empty, so maximality of $W$ gives $Z=Z_i$. Thus $Z$ is irreducible. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober] it has a unique generic point $s$. An open $O$ has empty $u$-value exactly when $O\subset W$, equivalently $O\cap Z=\varnothing$, equivalently $s
otin O$. Finally, for any etale $T	o S$, its image $O$ is open by [def-weil-etale-morphism, lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open], and $\{T	o O\}$ is a covering. The map $u(T)	o u(O)$ and joint surjectivity give $u(T)
e\varnothing$ exactly when $s$ lies in that image.

source.place: Tag 04HU, lemma-points-small-etale-site; second paragraph, with the sober-space argument of sites.tex Tag 04EJ written out.

proof.text: Choose an affine open $A\subset S$ containing $s$. Then $u(A)$ is a singleton. Restrict $u$ to the small etale site of $A$, regarding its objects as etale $S$-schemes; this is legitimate by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. The restricted functor still preserves finite limits and sends covers to jointly surjective families, with terminal value $u(A)=\{*\}$. Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(s)$ by [lem-pc-algebraic-closure-exists-unique]. The description in [def-weil-geometric-point] gives a geometric point $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to A\to S$ over $s$. All later affine objects used for the finite-fibre argument map to this fixed affine base $A$.

source.place: Tag 04HU, lemma-points-small-etale-site; second and third paragraphs, making the affine-base restriction explicit.

proof.text:
For an affine etale $A$-scheme $U$, apply [lem-trf-affine-etale-split-neighbourhood] at $\bar s$ to obtain an affine $(V,\bar v)$ and $U\times_A V=(\coprod_{i=1}^n V)\amalg W$, with no point of $W$ mapping to $s$. Step 2 gives $u(W)=\varnothing$ and $u(V)\ne\varnothing$. By step 1 and preservation of fibre products,
$$u(U)\times u(V)\simeq\coprod_{i=1}^n u(V)$$
over $u(V)$. Taking the fibre over any $b\in u(V)$ shows that $u(U)$ has exactly $n$ elements. If $U$ is a pointed neighbourhood of $\bar s$, step 2 also shows $u(U)\ne\varnothing$. This includes $n=0$: in that case $u(U)$ and the geometric fibre are both empty.

source.place: Tag 04HU, lemma-points-small-etale-site; third paragraph (finite cardinality of affine fibre values).

proof.text: Take the full category of affine pointed neighbourhoods of $\bar s$ which factor through $A$. It has a small skeleton $\mathcal J$: [lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-essentially-small-cover] gives a set of affine etale $A$-objects, and the lifts of $\bar s$ into each form a set. It is cofiltered. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered] on $A$ provides common sources and equalizers among all pointed neighbourhoods; take an affine open containing the marked point in each such source to remain among affine objects. The same refinement shows nonemptiness. For $(V,\bar v)\in\mathcal J$, the sets $u(V)$ are finite nonempty by step 4. Apply [lem-trf-cofiltered-finite-sets-section] to the covariant diagram $(V,\bar v)\mapsto u(V)$. Obtain elements $x_{V,\bar v}$ compatible with every pointed arrow; surjectivity of transition maps is not assumed.

source.place: Tag 04HU, lemma-points-small-etale-site; fourth paragraph (small cofiltered limit and compatible choice).

proof.text:
Extend this family to every pointed etale $S$-neighbourhood $(T,\bar t)$ as follows. Refine it by pulling back the open $A$, then taking an affine open around its marked point, and replacing it by an isomorphic object of $\mathcal J$. For such a pointed arrow $a:(V,\bar v)\to(T,\bar t)$ set $x_{T,\bar t}=u(a)(x_{V,\bar v})$. This is independent of the refinement: for two refinements use [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered] to find a common source, equalize its two resulting arrows into $T$, and refine that source to an affine object over $A$. Compatibility in $\mathcal J$ makes the two images equal. The same argument applied to a refinement and its composite with a pointed arrow shows $u(f)(x_{T,\bar t})=x_{T',\bar t'}$ for every pointed $f:(T,\bar t)\to(T',\bar t')$. Consequently
$$c_T:\operatorname{Hom}_S(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega,T)\to u(T),\qquad \bar t\mapsto x_{T,\bar t},$$
is natural in all etale $T$, not only the affine ones.

source.place: Tag 04HU, lemma-points-small-etale-site; last three paragraphs, replacing the omitted independence and functoriality checks by coherent neighbourhood elements.

proof.text: For $U$ affine over $A$, use the splitting of step 4 and take $b=x_{V,\bar v}$. Let $a_i:V\to U$ be the maps obtained from its $n$ copy sections and the projection. The final clause of [lem-trf-affine-etale-split-neighbourhood] says that $\bar u_i=a_i\bar v$ exhaust all geometric lifts into $U$, without repetitions. Compatibility from step 6 gives $c_U(\bar u_i)=u(a_i)(b)$. The fibre over $b$ of the isomorphism of step 4 sends its $i$-th point precisely to $u(a_i)(b)\in u(U)$. Therefore these elements exhaust $u(U)$ without repetitions. Thus $c_U$ is bijective, also for an empty fibre.

source.place: Tag 04HU, lemma-points-small-etale-site; last paragraph, explicit bijectivity on affine objects.

proof.text: For an arbitrary etale $T\to S$, put $T_A=T\times_S A$. Since $u(A)$ is a singleton, finite-limit preservation identifies $u(T_A)$ with $u(T)$; geometric lifts into $T_A$ and $T$ also agree because $\bar s$ factors through $A$. Cover $T_A$ by affine opens, as in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-essentially-small-cover]. Joint surjectivity of their $u$-values and step 7 give surjectivity of $c_{T_A}$. For injectivity, lifts $t_1,t_2$ with equal $c$-images factor through affine opens $B_1,B_2$. Their corresponding elements in $u(B_1)$ and $u(B_2)$ have the same image in $u(T_A)$, so define an element of $u(B_1\times_{T_A}B_2)$. Lift that element along an affine open cover of this fibre product to an element of some $u(C)$ with $C$ affine over $A$. Bijectivity of $c_C$ gives a geometric lift into $C$. By naturality its images in $B_1,B_2$ have the same $c$-images as the original lifts; injectivity of $c_{B_1},c_{B_2}$ identifies them with those lifts. Their composites in $T_A$ coincide, proving $t_1=t_2$. Thus $c$ is a natural isomorphism on the whole site. No affineness of the overlap is asserted.

source.place: Tag 04HU, lemma-points-small-etale-site; claim that affine objects suffice, whose proof the source omits; full cover argument.

proof.text:
The natural bijections $c_T$ identify the category of geometric pointed neighbourhoods with $\mathcal N_u$ of [lem-trf-site-point-reconstruction-sets], keeping underlying objects $T$ and arrows fixed. Reindexing its colimit formula therefore gives, naturally in every set sheaf $F$,
$$p^{-1}F\simeq\varinjlim_{(T,\bar t)\in\mathcal N_{\bar s}^{\mathrm{op}}}F(T).$$
By [lem-fix-geometric-stalk-topos-point] in its etale case, this is the inverse image of the actual point associated to $\bar s$. Its adjunction and the given adjunction for $p$ identify the right adjoints as well: the natural inverse-image isomorphism has its invertible right-adjoint mate as specified in [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. Hence $p$ is isomorphic to this geometric point. All indexing categories, field choices, and colimits lie in the common enlarged universe of the statement.
